title: Guarantee Execution
coreMove: Test agreement against implementation details until fake commitment has nowhere to hide.
sourcePressure: The source ties the chapter to implementation, liar detection, follow-through, and commitment, while warning not to claim perfect lie detection or treat collaboration language as execution readiness.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must not make this generic productivity follow-up, project management, or certainty about another person's motives.

hook: A team agrees in a meeting and misses the deadline
tryThisNow: Ask who does what by when

exampleSpecs.audience: a maintenance planner confirming a contractor's promise before a sterile line goes offline
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed valve replacement could waste a batch worth six figures
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the planner asks how the contractor will stage certified parts before the shutdown and watches the promise fail when the part lot number is missing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stainless valve tag hanging from a sealed parts bin outside the gowning room

exampleSpecs.audience: an IT director testing whether the vendor's cutover commitment can actually execute
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents may miss storm alerts if the old and new systems do not overlap
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director asks who will send the live test to the Spanish-language list and when, revealing that the vendor has not imported the list
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a test-alert console with the Spanish list count showing zero

exampleSpecs.domain: commercial kitchen hood repair before a fire inspection
exampleSpecs.audience: a property manager verifying a tenant's assurance that repairs are handled
exampleSpecs.stakes: the restaurant may fail inspection and close for the weekend if the hood certificate is absent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager traces how a confident yes collapsed when she asked which technician would upload the certificate before noon
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grease-filter panel leaning against a tile wall below an inspection notice

exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatch supervisor checking a courier's claim that a new route is covered
exampleSpecs.stakes: a blood unit may arrive outside temperature range if nobody owns the second handoff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor asks how the courier will keep the logger in range during the pharmacy stop, exposing that the backup cooler is still at another depot
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a temperature logger blinking inside a red transport case

exampleSpecs.domain: festival electrical inspection for temporary stages
exampleSpecs.audience: a production manager confirming a contractor's ready-to-open claim
exampleSpecs.stakes: the gates cannot open if grounding certificates are missing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the production manager contrasts the contractor's confident yes with the moment a how question reveals nobody scheduled the grounding test
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a coil of stage cable beside a locked electrical panel at dawn

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse robotics installation at a fulfillment center
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead testing the integrator's promise before go-live
exampleSpecs.stakes: orders may jam for a full shift if manual exception lanes are not staffed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead asks the integrator to walk the first exception tote from scanner to human review, revealing that the review station has no badge access
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a yellow exception tote stopped under a scanner arch

skillTargets: test a verbal agreement through implementation questions
spot fake commitment without claiming certainty about motives
analyze which missing detail threatens execution
evaluate whether a follow-up checks readiness or merely nags

tryThisNowSpec: For one agreement you are relying on, ask the owner to walk you through the first physical handoff, named person, or required document before you treat the yes as real.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
